# Forms a verification library's run reaches

The task module runs every fixture through the public CLI in both HDL optimizer
modes on legacy, compact/portable and compact/GMP values; the generated-C sweep
(`tests/generated_c_frame_lint.rs`) compiles each one with `-Wall` and accepts
no warning. Expected outputs were checked against an independent
industry-standard simulator; the clause lines below are from
`SystemVerilog-1800-2009.txt`.

| Fixture | Clause and oracle |
| --- | --- |
| `unused_locals` | 6.21 L6901-6903: "Variables declared in an automatic task, function, or block are local in scope, default to the lifetime of the call or block and are initialized on each entry to the call or block". 8.6 L9766: "The lifetime of methods declared as part of a class type shall be automatic." String, class handle, chandle and process locals of class methods, automatic functions and an automatic task that nothing names after the declaration (a handle local beside a `$cast` destination, as in a library's `do_copy`); each call returns as if they were absent. |
| `wide_hierarchy_randomize` | 18.6.1 L30398-30399: "The randomize() method is a virtual function that generates random values for all the active random variables in the object, subject to the active constraints." 18.4 L29372-29373: "An object handle can be declared rand, in which case all of that object’s variables and constraints are solved concurrently with the variables and constraints of the object that contains the handle." A class with 40 derived classes (more than one dispatch chains) and a two-level chain under one of them, randomized through a base-class handle as a value, in an `if` condition and through a `rand` handle: the constraints of the object's own class hold. The task module also generates it without building and checks that the C nesting stays below the class count, so a class with hundreds of derived classes (a verification library's sequence items) stays within C compiler nesting limits. |
| `specialization_spellings` | 8.25 L10772-10776: "A specialization is the combination of a specific generic class with a unique set of parameters. Two sets of parameters shall be unique unless all parameters are the same as defined by the following rules: a) A parameter is a type parameter and the two types are matching types. ... All matching specializations of a particular generic class shall represent the same type." 8.25 L10754-10755: "Each specialization of a class has a separate set of static member variables". A type reaches `typeid #(T)` through two spellings (`typeid #(CB)` in one `callbacks` specialization, `typeid #(T)` in the next, and a typedef), as a library's `uvm_typeid #(CB)` and `uvm_typeid #(T)` do: each pair names one specialization with one singleton, and seven singletons exist. `generated_c_determinism` also generates the fixture six times per optimizer mode: the spelling the frontend keeps for a specialization depends on which reference reached it first, which changes between runs, so the class order must not depend on it. |
| `recursive_rand_handle` | 18.4 L29372-29374: "An object handle can be declared rand, in which case all of that object’s variables and constraints are solved concurrently with the variables and constraints of the object that contains the handle. Randomization shall not modify the actual object handle." A base class with a recursive `rand` handle and 13 derived classes (one of them two levels deep); a chain of six objects of five classes (two of the base class) linked through the handle, randomized three times through a base-class handle: every linked object meets its own class's constraints and the chain is unchanged. The industry-standard simulator gives the same output and also warns that the last object's handle is null. |
| `recursive_rand_handle_wide` | Generation only, the form of `recursive_rand_handle` with 20 derived classes: the task module checks that it generates within its time bound and that every unit links the handle once (`llg_cr_link` sites at most problems x units), whatever the number of classes the child can have. |
| `string_format_time_unit` | 20.4.2 L34318-34320: "It specifies how the %t format specification reports time information for the $write, $display, $strobe, $monitor, $fwrite, $fdisplay, $fstrobe, and $fmonitor group of system tasks." 21.3.3 L36741-36742: "The $swrite family of tasks is based on the $fwrite family of tasks and accepts the same type of arguments as the tasks upon which it is based"; L36751: "$sformat supports all the format specifiers supported by $display". 21.2.1.2 L36105-36107: "The %t format specification works with the $timeformat system task to specify a uniform time unit, time precision, and format for reporting timing information from various modules that use different time units and precisions." Table 20-3 L34373: the default `units_number` is the smallest time precision. A module with unit 1 us and a package with unit 1 ns (precision 1 ps): `%t` of `$time`/`$realtime` through `$swrite`, `$sformat`, `$sformatf` and a run-time format gives the `$display` text, 1000000 (ps) by default and 1500 ns under `$timeformat(-9, 0, " ns", 5)`. |
| `string_function_packed_outputs` | 13.4 L18751-18755: "Functions can have the same formal arguments as tasks. Function argument directions are as follows: input // copy value in at beginning output // copy value out at end inout // copy in at beginning and out at end". A string-returning automatic function with a 1-bit output formal and a static string-returning function with an `int` inout and a 4-bit output formal, called as an assignment's right-hand side, inside concatenations and from a class method with class-property actuals: each actual holds the formal's final value after the call, and the static function's formals keep their storage between calls. The industry-standard simulator gives the same output. |
